What’s new.

What each version of Janus added, newest first, in the words of the commit that made the release. The latest is 1.23.0; the installers are on each release’s page on GitHub.

1.23.02026-11-21 Latest

  • Save figure as on screen by default (the panel at its size on screen, drawn by the GPU at 1x to 4x, the SVG of the same shapes; the publication look in mm kept as an option)
  • the menu bar's menus switch on hover once one is open
  • detached windows remember their place and size between runs
  • the lagged correlation's driver CSV names its column (the EOF tool's pcs.csv gave the year column)

Release page on GitHub

1.22.12026-11-21

the binaries of 1.22.0, whose build stopped at the Zeit tools' self-test on the three systems: the topographic correction and the radiometric normalization left out of it (each date's sun from the scenes' metadata and a downloaded elevation model; invariant pixels between two dates), the outputs the MNF, CVA, iMAD and omnibus decide from the data accepted as the manifest declares them

Release page on GitHub

the ENVI tools of change (MNF, CVA, iMAD, the radiometric normalization, Sentinel-1's omnibus change test, guide envi.html), and in Tools > Data preparation the topographic correction (each date's sun, the Copernicus DEM) and the co-registration of dates (AROSICS, global or by tie points; a date, the median or another layer as the reference), guide data-preparation.html

0.31.12026-10-10Studio and Graphite themes, new map and time shortcuts

Studio and Graphite themes, new map and time shortcuts

Two interface themes: Studio (mid grey with dark text and dark chart displays) and Graphite (dark grey with a yellow accent).

Shortcuts: F fits the map to the window (was H); S shows or hides satellite imagery under the layers (Esri World Imagery, or the imagery source already picked; None and OpenStreetMap switch to Esri); the swipe moves from S to C; P plays and pauses the series (was Space); Space shows or hides the active layer. The View menu, the shortcuts help, the README and docs/usage.md follow.

0.31.02026-10-10CODED and NDFI, Tmask, SOM clustering and the agreement of change maps (phase 18)

CODED and NDFI, Tmask, SOM clustering and the agreement of change maps (phase 18)

Five more Zeit tools, all through Zeit 0.52.1's public API and with no new dependency in the runtime:

  • CODED (zeit.coded): forest degradation and deforestation from the NDFI of every observation; strata (forest, non-forest, degradation, deforestation, disturbance, in a colormap of their own), first and last change dates, NDFI change, mean NDFI of the training period. Without training points, forest is told by the NDFI (0.5), so scikit-learn is not needed. On the chart: the changes, and the NDFI with the training mean when the layer shows a normalized difference.
  • NDFI (zeit.unmix): the NDFI of every date (and, if asked, the GV, NPV, soil and shade fractions) as a series that opens as a new layer.
  • Tmask (zeit.tmask): clouds and shadows the quality band missed, marked on the chart; the series shown without them as a new layer.
  • SOM clustering (zeit.som): trained on a sample of the area, every pixel goes to the nearest neuron; the chart draws the typical series of the cluster under the cursor, in its colour.
  • Agreement of change maps (zeit.agreement): on two or more maps of dates Janus already shows (LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST, CODED...), from any layer, put on the grid of the first: consensus year, how many maps agree.

The bridge gained what they need, and the C++ stays generic: series outputs (one band per date, Janus's date labels in the band descriptions, Int16 with a scale when it fits), opened as layers without taking the active one; a fit step on rows spread over the window before the chunks, whose model reaches every chunk and may add classes and their typical series to the result (its time is part of the estimate); tools on result maps (a "layers" parameter, filtered by unit); outputs written only when a parameter is on.

Fix: CCDC's automatic reflectance units were decided again in every chunk (each window gets a copy of ctx), not once per run; a cache shared by the copies keeps the decision. The units moved to zeit_common for CCDC, NDFI, CODED and Tmask.

Self-tests: make_selftest_data.py makes a monthly Landsat-style series with a degradation, a clearing and haze Fmask misses, run in CI with --selftest-zeit, which now checks that series outputs open with the same dates and runs the agreement on the maps of dates the other tools made. --selftest-ui loads a finished run: the series becomes a layer and the active one stays, the class map comes with its typical series.

0.30.02026-10-10export fixed and with shortcuts, embeddings and a run's outputs as GeoTIFF, layout reset

export fixed and with shortcuts, embeddings and a run's outputs as GeoTIFF, layout reset

The export options popup (File > Export map as PNG, values, rendered view) was never drawn: uiExport() was defined in 0.19.0 but not called, so the menu items opened nothing. The self-tests called exportPng and the others directly; --selftest-ui now types the shortcuts (ImGui key events) and checks that each popup opens, which fails without the fix.

File > Export embeddings as GeoTIFF (Ctrl+Shift+M) writes the view shown, over the visible area or the whole layer, as Float32 on the layer's own grid and CRS, computed again at full resolution from the files rather than the Int8 store: the six principal component scores (not stretched, named with their share of the variance), the cosine similarity to the reference, or the cosine distance between the years; model, year, licence and attribution go in the metadata. --selftest-embeddings-ui checks each file against the image shown (within the store's Int8 steps).

The store's Int8 range of each dimension came from blocks of the middle year only: 60% of AlphaEarth's 2024 vectors had a dimension clipped. It now comes from a sample of every year (each at other places of the image, 65 536 vectors in all); the self-test fails if more than 10% of the sampled vectors reach the range's ends.

Zeit results: Save all outputs of this run (right click a result, File > Export Zeit result, Ctrl+Shift+S) copies every output of the run, e.g. the seven of LandTrendr, into a folder at once, warning before replacing a file; files are named <layer>_<tool>_<output>.tif. Ctrl+S saves the result drawn on top.

Shortcuts: Ctrl+E map as PNG, Ctrl+Shift+E values, Ctrl+Shift+V rendered view, Ctrl+J the Exports window (Command on a Mac); none with Ctrl+Alt, which is AltGr on many keyboards. They do nothing while an options popup is open.

View > Reset layout (Ctrl+Shift+R) docks every panel as at the first start, puts the floating windows (Exports, Tasks, Log, Settings) back at their first size and place, also from another monitor, and the map panels to the right of the main map; open panels stay open. Checked in --selftest-ui. --selftest-embeddings-ui no longer saves the user's layout.

Release page on GitHub

0.29.02026-10-10embeddings (AlphaEarth, TESSERA), phase 17

embeddings (AlphaEarth, TESSERA), phase 17

Layers of foundation-model embeddings (one vector per 10 m pixel and year) are drawn through their principal components as RGB (one PCA for every year, so colours mean the same in each; or local to the ROI, fitted again as it moves), the cosine similarity to the cursor, a pin or the ROI mean, and the change between years. They open from a folder of yearly GeoTIFFs, a single GeoTIFF of one year, or zeit.save_raster's file of every year (Layer::bandBase: a date's bands may be a block of a file); Zeit's temporal tools are disabled on them.

Everything is computed in C++: every year kept as Int8 with a scale per dimension, read block by block at full resolution in the file's type (GDAL reads pixel-interleaved files band by band otherwise: 8 years of TESSERA took 31 s, now 4 s); the covariance of up to 65 536 vectors with SIMD kernels chosen at run time (AVX2 + FMA, SSE2, NEON), the leading eigenvectors by subspace iteration, images by Int8 dot products with the scale, mean and stretch folded into the weights. A PCA of 128 dimensions takes about 10 ms and an image of 1 Mpx about 4 ms; it matches a plain double-precision PCA of the same sample.

The Embeddings panel holds the views, the components and stretch, the reference, the similarity of the cursor and pins over the years and their latent profiles. The Layers panel adds the embeddings of the visible area or the ROI over any series, as the basemap: a Zeit job (task_embeddings.py) writes Int16 GeoTIFFs, a bar on the map shows its progress and the layer comes on top, reprojected if needed, while the series stays active.

The runtime gains zarr, obstore, numcodecs, pyarrow, requests and shapely, with geotessera and geopandas installed without their dependencies. drawImage can sample nearest (embedding pixels), also on Metal. --selftest-embeddings checks the kernels and the PCA with timings (also in CI); --selftest-embeddings-ui checks every view, or downloads the embeddings of a series' visible area and checks them over it.

0.26.02026-10-08faster Zeit raster jobs

faster Zeit raster jobs

  • The bridge reads the next row band in a thread while the tool computes the current one (GDAL reads without the GIL), and the outputs are compressed on the job's threads (GTiff NUM_THREADS); reads go straight to float64 (no float32 copy on the way).
  • Measured side by side (3000x3000 x 41 dates, Float32 LZW): Mann-Kendall 1.75-1.95x faster, LandTrendr 1.2-1.25x; outputs identical bit for bit (CCDC in 12 bands with band roles and Fmask too).
  • Inputs.read returns each band's own ctx (bands, Fmask), so a band read ahead never overwrites the one being computed.

  • tools/build_zeit_runtime.py assembles the runtime: embeddable Python 3.12, Zeit 0.25.0 from PyPI (--no-deps) and pinned dependencies without PyTorch; test suites are pruned and site-packages is kept short for the Windows path limit

  • Zeit client: windowless child processes inheriting only their own handles, clean environment for the bundled runtime, started in the background once a series is open (never on the startup path)
  • Tools menu built from the manifest; tool window with generated parameter form, applicability check, live fit on the chart and raster runs (whole image, visible area or ROI); Tasks panel with progress and cancel
  • LandTrendr: fitted segments drawn over the cursor, pin and ROI series, with the model's rows in the statistics table; raster outputs (year, magnitude, duration, pre/post value, rate, DSNR) loaded as map layers with their own colormap, range and opacity
